title: bug: contested-untouched landing skip silently drops a task's own Bash-written edit even when the contesting peer is idle and the path was clean at pre-flight
description:
Observed 2026-10-24: CQ-M01 (task-ad95cb27) completion baeacbf left out docs/CONFIGURATION.md, which is its own step-4/5 modifiedFiles. task.commits[].contested = [{docs/CONFIGURATION.md, task-07474ee4}], and QA rejected the task for the delivery gap at 16:39Z. The worker wrote the row via Bash, with `python3 - <<EOF ... s.replace(old,new)` at 16:18:19Z and 16:21:12Z. So the session's TOOL set lacked the path, and `attribution.contested: skip-untouched` (moe-agent.sh ~3564-3568, plus its ps1 twin) skipped it.

The contest was a false positive:
- The peer task-07474ee4 has been PLANNING and unassigned since 13:11Z, so no session could have written its bytes.
- Its claim is ASSERTED history whose bytes are already in HEAD (9f2cce3b).
- The path was clean at M01's pre-flight, so every dirty byte at exit came from M01's session.

Scale:
- 93 contested skips across task.commits history, mostly on the landing task's own asserted paths. For example, task-ca478039's completion dropped 6 own wrapper/test files on 2026-09-21.
- 07474ee4's month-old claims cover scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}, postflight.*, parity-check.*, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/SCHEMA.md.
- This is the same family as archived task-d1441364 (Serena tools missing from TOOL). Adding witness sources cannot cover Bash.

Suggested direction (the architect decides): treat a contested path as the session's own when both of these hold:
- it was clean in the landing session's pre-flight snapshot;
- the contesting peer task had no assignee active since that pre-flight (get_commit_scope already computes activity against `since`).
Keep skipping when the peer was live, or when the path was dirty at pre-flight and is untouched. That is the real unlanded-peer-hunks case.
definitionOfDone: Both wrappers (moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1) commit a landing task's own asserted path with no TOOL witness (e.g. a Bash/python edit) when that path was clean at the session's pre-flight and its only contesting peer task had no assignee active since that pre-flight.

A contested path is still skipped when the contesting peer's assignee was active since pre-flight, or when the path was already dirty at pre-flight and untouched by this session (existing postflight contested cases stay green).
A completion landing that still skips one of its own asserted paths names the path and the contesting peer in its #general session-ended line, so it is visible before QA.

New cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 fail on the old behaviour; fresh `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` and the daemon tests for any daemon file touched exit 0, with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Until this fix lands, edit the wrapper and test files with the Edit/Write tools, not Bash heredocs or python: task-07474ee4 contests scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} and scripts/tests/postflight.*, so an unwitnessed edit is silently left out of this task's own landing.
Keep moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 in parity; never weaken the live-peer or dirty-at-pre-flight skips.

implementationPlan.description:
SEAT CHECK FIRST, before any edit.
Six plan files are declared by seatless nonterminal peers:
- task-07474ee438f34021a23809f9c764d15c (PLANNING; plan + filesModified) declares scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/postflight.sh, scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/SCHEMA.md.
- task-e92b2cb33f744bf18074fc87121f22df (BACKLOG; plan) declares moe-agent.sh and both postflight harnesses.
The wrapper that lands THIS session still runs the OLD attribution. Under attribution.contested=skip-untouched, each of those six files lands ONLY with a TOOL witness. So make every edit in this plan with the Edit/Write tools (task rail), never Bash heredocs, sed or python.
A seat WITHOUT Edit/Write tools (codex/gemini/grok) must not edit anything. Call moe.report_blocked { blockedOnTaskIds: ['task-07474ee438f34021a23809f9c764d15c'], reason: 'needs an Edit/Write-capable seat: six plan files are contested by seatless peers; governor: unblock onto a Claude seat (resolveBlocks) or clear the stale contest' } and end the session.

Daemon half: per-path peer activity in moe.get_commit_scope (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts, LF). Load test-driven-development: write this step's tests first and watch them fail.
Each peerDeclared entry gains `peerActive: boolean`. A wrapper can then tell a contest by a task that cannot have written bytes during the landing session from one that may have.
- Add a helper, e.g. `peerTaskActive(state, other, nowMs, sinceMs)`. It returns true when ANY of these holds:
  - sinceMs is null (no window: stay conservative);
  - other.assignedWorkerId names a worker for which the existing isPeerActive(worker, nowMs, sinceMs) is true. A DEAD worker gives false; a missing worker record is not active by itself.
  - listAttempts(state, other.id) (state/attemptStore.ts) has an attempt whose phase is not 'closed';
  - an attempt's lastPhaseAt is unparsable or >= sinceMs - LIVENESS_TIMEOUT_MS (a session that ran and closed inside the window).
- Error handling: add no throw path. Every malformed or unparsable timestamp counts as active (fail closed). The tool stays read-only apart from the existing caller touch.
- Peers loop (~88-108): call the helper once per peer task. peerActive is an OR over EVERY nonterminal task that contributes the path, not only the first claimant (whose id stays in taskId):
  `const stored = peerSet.add(p); if (stored === null) continue; const entry = peerByKey.get(stored); if (entry) { entry.peerActive ||= active; continue; } peerByKey.set(stored, { path: stored, taskId: other.id, peerActive: active });`
  PathSet.add returns the already-stored spelling for a known key, so the lookup hits. The waitsOnThis rule (asserted paths only) is unchanged.
- livePeerIds, activePeerIds, peersActive and alwaysInclude are unchanged.
- Add one clause on peerActive to the tool description. The field is additive: an older wrapper ignores it.

Tests (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts). Add peerActive to the ScopeResult peerDeclared type, and assert exact booleans per path with toBe(true) / toBe(false):
(a) with since, an unassigned peer with no attempts -> false;
(b) the peer's assignee active at since-60s -> true; last active at since-10min and registered before since -> false; a DEAD assignee -> false;
(c) an unassigned peer with an open attempt (openAttempt) -> true; with an attempt closed (setAttemptPhase 'closed') inside the window -> true; with an attempt opened and closed long before since -> false. Control time with vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] }) + vi.setSystemTime, and restore with vi.useRealTimers;
(d) no since -> every entry true;
(e) two peers declare one path, the lower id idle and the other active -> ONE entry with taskId = the lower id and peerActive true. With the activity swapped -> still true.
Run `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts`.

Bash twin: the idle-peer exception in scripts/moe-agent.sh (LF). Edit/Write only, per step 1.

1. Pre-flight evidence (preflight_landing, ~5630-5637).
- Next to the MOE_PREFLIGHT_EVIDENCE copy, keep a private copy of THIS pre-flight's whole dirty snapshot ("$spre", rows of blob, xy, path) as MOE_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY="$(create_secure_temp)/preflight-dirty-$$.tsv". A failed copy leaves it empty.
- Keep it even when inherit_pre=1. The snapshot is always this session's, and a crashed session's unlanded bytes are dirty in it, so they stay held.
- Reset MOE_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY="" in the per-iteration block beside MOE_PREFLIGHT_EVIDENCE="" (~6091).
- MOE_PREFLIGHT_ISO (the `since` that commit_scope sends) is taken at the top of the iteration, before this snapshot, so the daemon's activity window covers it.

2. Plumbing.
- Declare LAND_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY="" beside LAND_EVIDENCE_FILE="" (~3348).
- run_landing (~5193-5200): set it to "" when LAND_RECOVERED=true (a recovery lands a dead session's bytes, whose window predates `since`), else to "${MOE_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY:-}".
- teardown_rescue (~5744): set it to "${MOE_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY:-}".
- resolve_attribution: pass MOE_LAND_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY="${LAND_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY:-}" into the python env. Keep the MOE_LAND_ prefix: parity-check compares the MOE_ATTR_/MOE_COMMIT_/MOE_CHECKPOINT_ code families, and MOE_LAND_* is sh-internal plumbing like MOE_LAND_EVIDENCE.

3. Python (resolve_attribution, ~3349-3600).
- PREFLIGHT_DIRTY = the set of key(norm_top(path)) over that file's rows, where path is the tab-joined parts[2:], exactly as S is read.
- PREFLIGHT_DIRTY is None when the env is empty or the file is missing or unreadable. Error handling there is fail closed: the exception is off.
- While building PEER, also build PEER_IDLE[k] = PEER_IDLE.get(k, True) and (ent.get('peerActive') is False). Only a JSON false is idle. Absent, null or anything else (an older daemon, the disk fallback, a duplicate entry) counts as active.
- In the skip-untouched branch (~3564), skip as today UNLESS all three hold:
  - PREFLIGHT_DIRTY is not None;
  - pk not in PREFLIGHT_DIRTY (clean at this session's pre-flight);
  - PEER_IDLE.get(pk) is True.
  When all three hold, fall through to the existing MOE_ATTR_ASSERTED_FOREIGN check and the ASSERTED candidate. The path stays in `contested`, so write_commit_message still records `Moe-Contested: <path> (<peer>)`.
- Rewrite the branch comment (ps1 twin) with the why. Every dirty byte at exit came from this session: the path was clean at its pre-flight, and no session of any contesting task ran since. A path that was already dirty at pre-flight stays held even if this session rewrote it, because it can carry the peer's earlier hunks.
- The 'skip' and 'commit' policies are unchanged.

4. Session-ended line (DoD 3).
- In run_landing, assign LAND_SUMMARY_HELD wherever LAND_SUMMARY_PATHS is assigned (grep every site). Use "" on the early-failure returns.
- On attributed landings, read "$ATTR_DIR/skipped" (NUL-separated code TAB path records).
- Each MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(<peer>) record becomes `<path>(<peer>)`. A bare MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED (policy skip) takes its peer from "$ATTR_DIR/contested" (peer TAB path records).
- Join the entries with ',', keep at most 5, then add `,+<N> more`.
- post_flight (~2490): after the outcome/code suffix, append " held=$LAND_SUMMARY_HELD" when it is non-empty, e.g. `... unattributed=0 held=contested.txt(task-peer)`.
- Error handling: an unreadable file gives an empty list and never fails the landing or the chat line.
- The text must be identical to the ps1 twin.

PowerShell twin in scripts/moe-agent.ps1. The file is LF with a UTF-8 BOM; keep both. Verify afterwards:

3. Get-MoeCommitScope (~2961-2992), rpc branch.

5. Held list.

MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(<peer>) becomes `<path>(<peer>)`; a bare MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED takes its peer from $attr.Contested. Use the same order, cap and `,+<N> more` as sh.

reopenReason: Governor-filed delivery-path bug, released to planning like b62c9fc7 and 709f6691. It is serialized behind b62c9fc7 because both edit moe-agent.{sh,ps1} and postflight.*.
planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 10 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected: (1) More TOOL witness sources: none can cover Bash or python writes; this is the same family as archived task-d1441364. (2) Judging 'clean at pre-flight' by the P rows (MOE_PREFLIGHT_EVIDENCE): P rows omit own-carried C bytes, and a pre-flight after an incomplete recovery inherits a dead session's P rows, whose window predates `since`. DoD 2 also says dirty-at-pre-flight paths stay held. The session's own full pre-flight snapshot is exact and aligned with `since` (MOE_PREFLIGHT_ISO is taken before the snapshot). (3) Wrapper-side peer activity from livePeerIds plus reading .moe/tasks: no attempt visibility, and get_commit_scope already measures activity against `since`. (4) Gating on the global peersActive: any unrelated live worker would block every release, which is the status quo the bug describes. (5) A separate docs task: this is the epic-final row and owns the docs sweep; four one-paragraph edits; the contract and the behaviour land together.

planningNotes.risks: (1) The worst failure is a wrong release that lands a live peer's hunks, which has torn the shared branch before. Defence: three ANDed conditions, fail-closed defaults (absent field, no since, unparsable timestamps, disk fallback, recovery) and the step 8 mutations. (2) A peer session that ended before since-120s and left unlanded hunks: those bytes are dirty at our pre-flight, so they stay held. (3) A human editing a clean path mid-session outside Moe would land under this task. That is the same assumption own_bytes/MEASURED already make. (4) This session's own landing runs the OLD wrapper: TOOL witnesses are required on the six contested files, and harnesses run from a snapshot. (5) b62c9fc7 (WORKING, same four script files) gates this task via dependsOn. Re-read its AC/AD and bump from the count that landed. (6) Windows PowerShell 5.1: the BOM, Set-Content encodings, .cmd quoting. (7) Own-carried (C-row) paths that are dirty at pre-flight stay held under the strict rule. The worker must Edit/Write-touch them, and held= makes them visible. This is deliberate per DoD 2.
